newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt, opposition agree TV licence extension.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt, opposition agree TV licence extension.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government and the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance reached a preliminary accord to extend broadcasting licences due to expire.

Party representatives reached the agreement after a meeting that ran into the early hours of Wednesday. If approved by parliamentary party leaders, an umbrella amendment extending licences until May 31, 1997 from January 31, 1997 will be presented to the Chamber of Deputies (lower house).

The agreement follows a prior decree approved in parliament last month to extend broadcasters' licences until the January deadline and mainly affects media tycoon and centre-right leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset television group.
The decree was issued in August, the day after expiry of a deadline set by Italy's constitutional court for a new legal framework on ownership to be put in place.

A December 1994 ruling said no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three channels and the government has presented a bill to shake up the sector but this has been held up by disagreement over a telecommunications section in the legislation.
